scope: Product-specific specialization of the approved conceptual ER model. The thirty approved use cases and their identifiers remain unchanged.
boundary: Logical documentation model, not an AWS database schema, SDK payload or shared runtime. Green means AWS defines the concept; it does not mean every green item has an independent ARN, CRUD API or equal availability. Relationship multiplicities are qualified individually and are not service quotas.

notation.range: Each relationship records targets per source and sources per target. 0..* means optional repeated association, not unlimited quota; ? means that exact multiplicity is not established by the reviewed guidance.
notation.basis: documented = relationship stated in the source; logical = useful documentation association inferred from described behavior, not a service foreign key; editorial = relationship introduced by this collection.
notation.identity: Only documented identifiers are named as API fields. Other identities are described by their console or application context. Composite identity descriptions in this file are documentation keys, not invented API parameters.
notation.ownership: The color classifies the definition of a concept, not who authors its content, pays for it or approves its use. IAM roles and EventBridge rules are AWS-defined dependencies outside the agent service.

entities.name: Agent Space
entities.meaning: Operational container for account access, integration associations, knowledge and executions.

entities.name: Provider registration
entities.meaning: Registered provider endpoint and authorization; registration alone does not select a space's tools.

entities.name: Service association
entities.meaning: Provider-specific configuration selecting the service resources or tools usable in that space.

entities.name: Selected tool
entities.identity: Tool identifier within its configured provider
entities.meaning: An exposed operation selected for use; not an independently deployed tool resource.

entities.name: Resource and operator IAM roles
entities.meaning: Separate roles govern service resource access and operator access; elevated action access is another role binding.

entities.name: Custom-agent definition
entities.meaning: Stored prompt with selected tools, skill asset IDs and memory-store asset IDs; not an invocation.

entities.name: Skill
entities.meaning: Procedural instructions and references with applicability and agent-type scope.

entities.name: Agent instructions
entities.meaning: Standing guidance loaded into new applicable work; content is not an IAM policy.

entities.name: Memory store
entities.meaning: Collection with a subject description; managed and custom stores have different write behavior.

entities.name: Memory entry
entities.identity: Memory asset identity within its store
entities.meaning: Synthesized informational content that can be selected and read for a task.

entities.name: Memory content version
entities.meaning: Immutable content revision; a version selector is not evidence of every possible restore or undelete operation.

entities.name: Custom-agent trigger
entities.identity: Trigger shown on the custom-agent definition
entities.meaning: Rate or cron schedule for future invocations; pausing it does not cancel existing work.

entities.name: Custom-agent invocation
entities.meaning: A particular execution with status, tool calls and outputs; its trajectory is execution detail.

entities.name: Incident signal
entities.identity: Signal linkage and displayed triage decision
entities.meaning: Incoming incident context can be linked, skipped or scheduled for independent investigation.

entities.name: Investigation
entities.meaning: Evidence-gathering work and evolving incident conclusions; not the same record as a signal.

entities.name: Investigation feedback
entities.meaning: Operator verdict and verified correction. Do not assume a one-to-one mapping to every internal reflection entry.

entities.name: Topology and environment understanding
entities.identity: Space, selected view and applicable knowledge version
entities.meaning: Discovered and inferred relationships; not an independent access boundary or a complete authoritative inventory.

entities.name: Prevention evaluation
entities.meaning: Analysis of investigation history for proposed improvements.

entities.name: Prevention recommendation
entities.meaning: Proposed improvement with a review state, not an implemented resource change.

entities.name: Directed-action approval
entities.identity: Approved operation, target and operator attribution
entities.meaning: Execution-time authorization separate from opt-in, role permissions and tool classification.

entities.name: Chat conversation
entities.identity: Conversation in the space web app
entities.meaning: On-demand inquiry and supported configuration/action requests do not inherently require a custom-agent definition.

entities.name: Release-readiness review
entities.identity: Review task and candidate source revision
entities.meaning: Change analysis is distinct from active testing of a deployed application.

entities.name: Release test profile
entities.meaning: Reusable target and test-type configuration; not the documentation implementation profile.

entities.name: Release test execution
entities.identity: Release Manager task or displayed test result
entities.meaning: Real requests and observed results; application data may change.

entities.name: Telemetry or repository source
entities.identity: Provider-native resource, revision and time range
entities.meaning: Original observations remain distinct from a copied summary or retained memory.

entities.name: Deployed application
entities.identity: Endpoint, deployed revision and test identity
entities.meaning: The target receives requests; accepting a test profile is not blanket authorization.

entities.name: Managed agent role
entities.identity: Agent type shown in Managed agents
entities.meaning: Platform-owned role; it is not a user-created custom_agent asset. Incident roles participate in investigations. Only Learning exposes its own run history and platform-owned triggers.

entities.name: Learning execution
entities.identity: Run selected in the Learning history
entities.meaning: Observable synthesis and refresh execution; do not infer a separately runnable record for every managed incident role.

View multiplicity is not an API inventory or authorization contract.
Actual provider operations and identity determine the readable scope.

Application writes are distinct from directed AWS API actions.
Approval applies to the operation and resource, not every subsequent message.
AWS-resource directed actions use the registered elevated role; permissions alone are not approval.
Roles are platform-owned, not custom-agent definitions.
This edge applies to Learning only; other managed roles execute within investigations.

entities.name: Shared service scope
entities.identity: Tenant/organization scope used in the guide
entities.meaning: The documented shared layer; do not equate it with a new AWS Organizations resource or infer cross-account policy propagation.

entities.name: Agent Space
entities.meaning: Groups application sources, settings, assignments and assessments.

entities.name: Integration registration
entities.meaning: Authorization registered before particular sources are connected to an application.

entities.name: Agent Space source connection
entities.meaning: Selects a repository or documentation source; per-capability settings decide its use.

entities.name: Repository or design source
entities.meaning: The original source can be reused across spaces without making every assessment identical.

entities.name: Security requirement pack
entities.meaning: Managed or custom collection governing subsequent eligible design and code reviews.

entities.name: Security requirement
entities.meaning: Applicability and compliance criteria, not an assessment result or certification.

entities.name: Penetration-test configuration
entities.meaning: Reusable target, scope, authentication and execution settings.

entities.name: Target and network rules
entities.identity: Rules within the selected test configuration
entities.meaning: Target, supporting access and excluded paths have different permitted effects.

entities.name: Test credential definition
entities.meaning: Credential strategy and login instructions; obtaining a secret is distinct from authentication.

entities.name: Retained login procedure
entities.identity: Procedure associated with the configured authentication flow
entities.meaning: Reuse of successful navigation; no independent editable skill-resource API is asserted.

entities.name: Penetration-test run
entities.identity: Run identity, target revision and observed credentials
entities.meaning: Independent execution against the target as it exists at run time.

entities.name: Penetration-test finding
entities.meaning: Retains vulnerability evidence and identity through repair and repeated revalidation.

entities.name: Revalidation job
entities.identity: Job in run history with type Revalidation
entities.meaning: Retests selected evidence; it neither replaces the original finding nor performs broad discovery.

entities.name: Finding-to-revalidation result
entities.identity: Our pair: original finding and revalidation job
entities.meaning: Captures the reported result for a selected finding. This is not asserted to be a separate AWS API resource.

entities.name: Full-code review configuration
entities.identity: Selected source configuration and repository settings
entities.meaning: Reusable selection of repositories or S3 sources for full scans; repository-event review settings are modeled separately.

entities.name: Code review
entities.meaning: A source assessment is not a running-application test.

entities.name: Design review
entities.meaning: Analyze submitted design material once; clone creates a new review rather than rerunning the same object.

entities.name: Threat-model configuration
entities.meaning: Reusable source and scope selection with on-demand runs.

entities.name: Threat-model run
entities.identity: Run identity within a threat model
entities.meaning: Produces a system overview and threats for that run; inferred boundaries need review.

entities.name: Remediation attempt
entities.meaning: Finding-linked attempt to produce a code proposal; it is not the repository settings or the resulting deployment.

entities.name: Patch or pull request
entities.identity: Diff or provider-native pull request and revision
entities.meaning: A proposal requires review, tests and deployment before a repair can be tested.

entities.name: Deployed test application
entities.identity: Endpoint, deployment revision and actual test role
entities.meaning: Actual application state may differ from the repository branch or earlier run.

entities.name: Jira integration and project connection
entities.meaning: Destination authorization is separate from source access and assessment execution.

entities.name: Jira issue
entities.meaning: External finding handoff; disconnecting an integration is not issue deletion.

entities.name: Repository code-review settings
entities.meaning: Controls eligible change review, selected analysis modes and comments. These settings are not the full-scan configuration.

entities.name: Remediation repository settings
entities.identity: Eligible source repositories and feature settings
entities.meaning: Determines where supported fix proposals can be created. Settings alone do not represent a remediation attempt.

entities.name: Code-review finding
entities.identity: Review identity, source revision and finding location
entities.meaning: Static-analysis result with source evidence. Penetration-test revalidation is not inferred for this result type.

relationships.note: Scope hierarchy from the guide, not an AWS Organizations API schema.
Provider-specific setup precedes selecting application sources.
Connection scope is application-specific.
A repository can be connected to multiple spaces. Provider-level connection grouping is not forced to one repository.
Requirements affect future eligible reviews across spaces, not past results.
Each requirement belongs to a pack; custom packs may be created before adding requirements.
Different test targets or scopes can have separate definitions.
Create once, execute repeatedly; runs are independent.
Multiple credentials can represent different application roles; reuse constraints are not generalized.
Rule collections are members of configuration, not independently authorized workloads.
The guide documents reuse, not an exact procedure-to-credential schema or separate skill management API.
An absence of findings does not establish complete authenticated coverage.
Normalized lineage association; each pair records one finding's result for one job.
A job selects one or more findings. Pending or failed work may not yet have a conclusive result value.
This relationship describes full scans. Repository-event reviews originate through their own connected-source settings.
New reviews may originate without a clone. This is a logical derivation, not a claimed clone-parent API field.
Reusable configuration is distinct from its system overview and threat results.
Selected review modes and current pack enablement matter; existing reviews do not change retrospectively.
Shared requirements do not imply a mutable result shared between applications.
Eligible automatic or manual remediation remains distinct from deployment.
The output depends on provider and repository support; not every attempt succeeds.
Target reachability, role and deployed revision must be recorded per run.
Repair must reach the original environment; current authentication is used.
When linked, revalidation can add a result comment. No universal one-issue-per-finding rule is asserted.
Provider-specific events and source revision identify the change-review path.
Provider eligibility and the accepted finding remain required.
Keep source-review results distinct from running-application findings.

entities.name: FinOps agent instance
entities.identity: finops-agent AgentSpace actions and agentspace ARN in IAM
entities.meaning: Independent instance in the UI. Its AgentSpace API/IAM name does not make it a DevOps Agent Space.

entities.name: Agent data role
entities.identity: IAM role ARN trusted by finops-agent.amazonaws.com
entities.meaning: Permits cost and operational reads and the managed-rule operations required for event automations.

entities.name: Operator role
entities.meaning: Distinct from the agent data role and from the end user's own entry permissions.

entities.name: Integration registration
entities.meaning: Registers authorization before an instance is connected to a project or channel.

entities.name: Agent connection
entities.identity: Connection to selected integration and destination
entities.meaning: Binds the registered integration to the selected Jira project or Slack channel.

entities.name: Conversation
entities.meaning: Can answer directly. A conversation is not automatically a task.

entities.name: Task
entities.meaning: On-demand, scheduled or event-created execution with recorded results.

entities.name: Automation
entities.identity: Saved automation in the Automations workspace
entities.meaning: Schedule or supported event condition that creates new tasks.

entities.name: EventBridge managed rule
entities.meaning: Delivers matching Cost Anomaly Detection events; it is not a general customer event orchestration API.

entities.name: AWS cost and operational evidence
entities.identity: Original query basis, anomaly or recommendation identifier
entities.meaning: Our grouping of distinct AWS-source results: cost query, forecast, coverage, anomaly, recommendation and change event. It is not one FinOps resource type or a shared evidence API.

entities.name: Context file
entities.meaning: Operator-maintained reference; the agent can read but not rewrite or delete it conversationally.

entities.name: Persistent memory
entities.identity: Preference, fact or correction addressed in conversation
entities.meaning: Supports remember, update and forget; no DevOps-style attachment or version API is inferred.

entities.name: Session runtime
entities.identity: Current session context, not an asserted public resource ID
entities.meaning: Loads retained files into an isolated runtime. Ending a session does not delete persistent records.

entities.name: Conversation summary
entities.identity: Older-message summary within the current conversation context
entities.meaning: Compaction is distinct from persistent memory and does not promise verbatim retention.

entities.name: Report artifact
entities.meaning: Generated report that can be inspected, revised, downloaded or deleted independently of external copies.

entities.name: Jira approval decision
entities.identity: Requested Jira action and invocation context
entities.meaning: Not required per action for pre-authorized automations; Slack does not use this prompt.

entities.name: Jira project or Slack channel
entities.meaning: Publication has its own authorization, membership and retention rules.

entities.name: Published issue, comment or message
entities.identity: Provider-native issue, comment or message identity
entities.meaning: A service result copied externally has a lifecycle separate from the originating task or artifact.

relationships.note: One configured role responsibility; do not infer that customer-managed roles cannot be referenced elsewhere.
Separate permission responsibility from data access and end-user entry.
Actual supported connection quotas are separate from logical multiplicity.
Registration is at account level; connection is at instance level.
Connection binds the intended project or channel. This is not evidence of reading all destination content.
Conversation history is instance-local.
The shared task queue belongs to this instance, not to all agents in the organization.
An automation is not an already-created task.
A task may instead be on demand. No universal automation ID field is asserted by this logical relationship.
Direct answers do not require a task, and Tasks workspace is another initiation path.
Exact rule-to-automation cardinality is not specified; do not assert one rule per automation.
Files are visible to users with agent access, and soft deletion changes active context.
No independent customer-managed memory-store schema is documented here.
Runtime isolation is not deletion of the retained input.
No cross-instance shared memory is inferred.
Summary representation and revision count are not exposed as a customer-managed resource model.
Artifacts can also originate from direct conversations. Do not force every artifact to have exactly one task parent.
Jira and Slack actions have different approval behavior; delivery success must be inspected separately.
Query dimensions, time basis and source identity govern the meaning of returned values.
